plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' bids. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying relative to my valuation. Since my value is $13, I will bid $13 to ensure truthful bidding, which guarantees non-negative profit if I win and no loss if I lose.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. With value $15, bidding exactly $15 ensures I win whenever profitable (when others bid below $15) and pay less than my value, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With value $47, I should bid exactly $47 to maximize expected profit.
